rules.statement: The Court of Appeal can exercise its powers of revision even when an appeal is not available, especially in exceptional circumstances where non-interference would cause a denial of justice or irremediable harm.
rules.supporting_quote: "Where the law does not give a right of appeal and makes the order final, the Court of Appeal may nevertheless exercise its powers of revision, but it should do so only in exceptional circumstances. Ordinarily the Court will, not interfere by way of review, particularly when the law has expressly given an aggrieved party an alternate remedy such as the right to file a separate action except when non-interference will cause a denial of justice or irremediable harm."

meta.parties: Rasheed Ali v. Mohamed Ali and Others
